when: before 1:30
asks: where do I start
they might invade, which buff
should I change my start
do I start red or blue
they showed at my buff level one
say: Hold near mid until camps are almost up, then start the buff they didn't show at, or keep your normal start if nobody showed.
more: Buffs spawn at 0:55, so waiting a few seconds in the middle costs nothing. A jungler who commits early to one side is the one a late invade catches.
If they take one of your buffs, take the buff of theirs on the same side of the map, or just clear your other half. Both junglers then farm opposite sides.
A split map decides which of your lanes gets help for the first few minutes. Tell the lane on the far half that you won't be there.
check: Did any enemy show on a ward or arrive late to a lane, and which of your laners can walk over first?
breaks: Wrong if your champion needs a leash to clear healthily and your team is already waiting at a buff: start there with them instead.
basis: pro:Wait in the middle and read the late invade

when: before 4:00
asks: my jungler's getting invaded, do I go
should I help at the buff
jungler pinged help, leave the wave?
do I drop my wave for my jungler
say: Go now and give up the wave if you can reach the buff first, or stay and ping him off if their mid is already moving.
more: A buff fight in the first clear is usually decided by the first laner to arrive, not by the two junglers. A few minions cost less than your jungler's buff and his Flash.
If you save him, he keeps his clear and you get help back sooner. If he dies there, their jungler owns that half of the map and your lane is next.
Their mid gets a free push while you're gone, so expect to lose some minions under tower when you come back.
check: How far is the fight from you, is their mid already walking, and is your jungler healthy enough to live until you arrive?
breaks: Wrong if their mid has the wave pushed and left first: you arrive second into a fight you lose. Hold the wave and tell your jungler to leave.
basis: pro:Drop the wave to win the buff fight

when: your mid laner is level 4 or 5
asks: who do I gank
should I gank mid
mid's losing lane, help him?
is mid worth a gank before six
say: Gank mid now just to burn Flash, so your mid laner can kill at six, or path bot if their mid's hugging tower.
more: A mage with no Flash can't dodge an all-in. If your mid has kill pressure at level 6, the Flash you burn now becomes a solo kill a minute or two later.
You don't need the kill. Force the Flash, help shove the wave so your mid gets a recall, and go back to your camps.
The trade-off is that their jungler gets the side you left. Decide before you walk in whether a Flash is worth one camp rotation.
check: Does their mid still have Flash, where is the mid wave, and can your mid laner really follow up with a kill at six?
breaks: Wrong if your mid can't kill alone at six anyway, like a farming mage: put the gank where a kill or tower plates are more likely.
basis: pro:Burn the Flash before your mid hits six

when: you just reached level 6
asks: I'm six, can I kill him
do I all in now
I just hit six what do I do
can I go on their mid
say: If his Flash is down, all-in as soon as he steps up for a minion, or shove and roam if he still has it.
more: Level 6 is the biggest gap you get in lane against a mage. Without Flash he has no way to leave once you're on him.
Pick the moment he uses a spell on the wave. He has to choose between farming and holding it for you, and either way he gives something up.
If he keeps Flash, the fight costs your ultimate for his Flash. Using that ultimate in a side lane often pays more.
check: Was his Flash used in the last few minutes, is his jungler showing somewhere else, and is the wave on your side?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is unseen and the wave is at his tower: you get turned on. Hold the wave near your side and wait for him to walk up.
basis: pro:Level six against a mid with no Flash

asks: who tanks the tower
do I go in first on the dive
how do we dive him
who takes tower aggro
say: Let the tankiest player with an escape step in first and hold the tower, then the damage goes in, or back off if nobody can.
more: The tower keeps shooting the first player it targets until he leaves. If that player can dash out, your killer gets a few free seconds.
Whoever holds the tower doesn't need to deal damage. Stand at the edge, take the shots, and leave before it gets dangerous.
A clean dive usually pays twice: the kill, then the wave and plates while he walks back.
check: Is a big wave under the tower with you, who has a dash or shield to leave with, and where is their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if the target still holds a stun or an untargetable spell and you have no minions: let the wave bounce and wait for the next big one.
basis: pro:The tank holds the tower from the edge

when: an enemy in your lane died in the last 15 seconds
asks: we killed him under tower, now what
do we recall or take plates
got the kill bot, stay or back
dive worked, what next
say: Recall straight away if the wave is about to bounce back, or stay for plates only if a fresh wave is arriving with you.
more: After a dive your minions die to the tower and the wave pushes back toward you. That gives you a safe recall and a wave waiting when you return.
Staying low on health with no minions invites their jungler and the respawned laner. That is how a clean kill turns into a traded one.
Buying first means the next fight in lane is on your items. A lead grows when it is spent, not while you carry it.
check: How many of your minions are left, how healthy are you both, and is another wave about to reach the tower?
breaks: Wrong if both enemies died and a full wave is with you: take the plates first, then recall together.
basis: pro:After a dive the wave bounces back

asks: it's two versus one top
they sent two top, what do I do
I can't farm, they're both here
how do I lane against two
say: Stay just close enough for experience and only take minions at your tower, or ask your jungler for help if they dive.
more: Against two you can't win a trade, so the lane is measured in how little you lose. Levels matter more than gold here because levels keep you alive under tower.
While two of them are on you, one of your other lanes has an easier time. Your team should be taking something there.
They usually leave after the first plates. If you're within a level of your lane opponent by then, you held the lane.
check: How big is the wave they're building, do you have Teleport to come back, and is their jungler joining for a dive?
breaks: Wrong if they stack a big wave with their jungler nearby: step away from the tower early and give the wave rather than die with it.
basis: pro:One against two, lose as little as possible

when: Teleport is one of your spells
asks: should I tp to that fight
do I teleport in
they're fighting mid, do I tp
tp or keep pushing
say: Teleport only if you land before the first kill and they have no answer, or keep pushing and take the tower if it's already decided.
more: A Teleport into a fight that's half over usually buys a one for one. Meanwhile their side laner takes your tower for free.
Teleport is also what lets you sit in a side lane when the next objective spawns. Spend it on a small trade and you have to stand with the team for minutes.
If you stay, make the push count: a tower or a deep wave pulls one of them away from whatever they wanted to do next.
check: Is the fight even or already lost, does their side laner have Teleport up, and what spawns in the next two minutes?
breaks: Wrong if the fight is over Baron or a soul-point dragon: go, even late, because that objective outweighs the tower.
basis: pro:A Teleport for a one for one loses a tower

when: your health is low and a dragon is up or spawns within a minute
asks: I'm low, do I back
should I recall now or get the wave
dragon's coming and I'm low
can I stay for one more wave
say: Recall now while the wave is neutral so you're back for dragon, or stay only if you have Teleport to return.
more: A mid laner forced out of lane right before a dragon gives it away. Nobody on your team can walk into the river with their mid already standing there.
Recalling one wave early costs a few minions. Being forced out thirty seconds later costs the same minions plus the dragon.
With Teleport you can afford the greedy wave, because you return to lane before he can do much with the push.
check: Is their support or jungler hovering mid, how many minions would you lose, and is your Teleport up?
breaks: Wrong if a big wave is about to hit your tower: clear it from max range first, then recall, or you lose the wave and tower health too.
basis: pro:A mid forced out gives the dragon

when: their mid laner does not have Teleport
asks: can I roam mid
when do I leave lane as support
should I go help mid
is it a good time to roam
say: Roam mid with the next big wave to chunk their mid if he has no Teleport, or stay if your carry's alone against two.
more: A mid laner without Teleport who is forced to recall loses a wave and often the river. You don't need a kill, only a big piece of his health.
Arriving with a cannon wave means he has to stand near the minions to farm. That's when a support's crowd control lands.
It sets up the next dragon: their mid is in base or low, so your jungler can start it with nobody able to answer first.
check: Is your bot wave pushed or your carry in base, and can your own mid laner follow up when you arrive?
breaks: Wrong if your bot wave is frozen near their tower: your carry loses more than the roam gains. Fix the wave first.
basis: pro:The support chunks a mid who cannot teleport back

when: the enemy team has Pantheon or Galio at level 6
asks: where do I go next
should I cover bot
my lane's pushed up, do I stay near
what do I do after this camp
say: Stand behind your pushed lane while their long-range ultimate is up, or farm the far side if that lane agrees to play back.
more: Pantheon and Galio can both land on a fight from far away. A lane that's pushed up goes from even numbers to one short with almost no warning.
If you're there when it lands, the numbers are even again and they spent an ultimate for nothing. That's a fair price for a few seconds of hovering.
Don't hover for long. If the ultimate shows somewhere else, go straight back to your camps or the nearest objective.
check: Has that ultimate been used recently, is your lane really past the middle, and which camps are you giving up?
breaks: Wrong if their Pantheon or Galio just used the ultimate elsewhere: the lane is safe for a while, so take camps or an objective instead.
basis: pro:Stand behind the lane a global can land on

when: the enemy team has Pantheon or Galio at level 6
asks: can I push side
is it safe to split
should I go bot lane alone
how far can I push
say: Push only as far as your side of the river while their long-range ultimate is up, or go deep right after it's used.
more: With Pantheon or Galio alive, a duel in a side lane can become one against two very quickly. Their side laner only has to hold you in place.
The window is right after that ultimate is spent. Then the side lane really is a duel, and you can take the tower or force two more to come.
If you can't see them, shove the wave past the middle and step back into fog. The wave still pulls someone without you standing in it.
check: When did you last see that ultimate used, do you have Flash, and is a teammate close enough to help?
breaks: Wrong if your team is about to fight an objective one player short: stop pushing and be there, or have Teleport ready.
basis: pro:Side lanes against a team with global ultimates

when: a dragon or Baron spawns within 40 seconds and you are holding a lot of gold
asks: do I back for my item
I've got gold, recall before dragon?
can I buy first
item or dragon
say: Too late to recall: go to the pit on what you have, or give this one cleanly and buy if it isn't soul point.
more: An item that finishes after the dragon is dead bought nothing for that fight. Worse, your team walks in one at a time while you run from base.
If you decide to give it, say so early so nobody else goes. Then spend, clear the camps on the other side and be first to the next one.
The recall belonged a minute before the spawn. Next time, base as soon as the previous fight ends.
check: How long until the spawn, is your team already at the pit, and how many dragons do they have?
breaks: Wrong if the enemy isn't near the pit and your waves are pushed: then a quick recall is free, so take it.
basis: pro:An item that arrives after the fight

when: after 20:00 and two or more enemies died in the last 20 seconds
asks: do we do baron
we got two kills, baron?
can we take baron now
what do we do after that fight
say: Start Baron only if your jungler and damage are healthy and their timers are long, or take a tower and reset if you're low.
more: Baron hits hard. A team that won a fight on low health can lose it to the survivors and one Smite. Kills only open Baron if you can still fight afterwards.
The safe conversion is a tower plus a full recall. You come back with items and vision, and Baron is still there after the next pick.
Check who died. If their jungler is alive, he only needs one Smite. If he's dead, even a slow Baron is safe.
check: What is your team's health, is their jungler among the dead, and how long until the first enemy respawns?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is dead with a long timer and your carry is healthy: start it at once, even at medium health.
basis: pro:Kills without health are not a Baron

when: after 14:00
asks: which side lane do I take
top or bot for me
who should I match in side
where do I go after laning
say: Take the side lane where their squishy laner stands so you can threaten a kill, or swap with a teammate if you're facing a tank.
more: A duelist who pushes into a tank kills nobody and gets killed by nobody. The lane is wasted for both, and your team loses its main threat.
Against a mage or a carry in the side lane, your wave pressure comes with kill pressure. They must send a second player, which opens the map for your team.
Ask for the swap with pings as soon as the lanes break up. It gets harder once towers fall.
check: Which enemy is in each side lane, do they have Flash, and can the teammate you swap with hold the other matchup?
breaks: Wrong if the squishy laner's side has no vision and their jungler is near: take the safer lane and just hold the wave.
basis: pro:Pick the side lane by who is standing in it

when: your team killed the Rift Herald in the last two minutes
asks: where do I use herald
which tower for herald
herald mid or side
should I save herald
say: Drop Herald on the tower your team can't break by itself, usually mid against wave clear, or on a low side tower for sure gold.
more: A short-range team can't siege a tower defended by a mage who clears waves. Herald is the one tool that hits it without your team standing in poke.
With mid tower down, both rivers open up. Their wave clear no longer guards the way to dragon and Baron.
If mid is full health and a side tower is nearly dead, the guaranteed tower is fine. A Herald killed before it charges is worth nothing.
check: How much health is on each outer tower, who defends mid, and can they kill Herald before it charges?
breaks: Wrong if three or more enemies are waiting mid: use it in a side lane where one defender can't stop it.
basis: pro:Use Herald on the tower you cannot siege

when: before 6:00 and your lane is behind in CS
asks: we're getting bullied bot
they keep poking us out
can't walk up to the wave
how do we survive this lane
say: Let them push, farm at your tower and recall when low, or call your jungler once their wave is stuck at your tower.
more: A poke lane wins by getting you low under tower and then diving with the jungler. If you're healthy under tower, the dive fails and they are the ones overextended.
An early recall refills health and mana. Dying with gold in your pockets is how the lane actually gets lost.
Most bully lanes fall off around your level 6 and first item. Being a wave or two behind at that point is a fine result.
check: Is a big wave building for a dive, where was their jungler last seen, and is there a ward in the brush behind you?
breaks: Wrong if they stop pushing and hold the wave near their tower: then you need your jungler to break it, or you lose all the experience.
basis: pro:Outlast the lane that wants to dive you

when: a dragon or Baron spawns within a minute
asks: should I go ward
do I ward the pit now
can I check that bush
where do I ward for dragon
say: Ward only as far as a teammate can follow right now, or wait at the river entrance until your team's back from base.
more: A support who dies checking brush alone gives the objective away before it starts. Your team is then one short and missing its engage or its peel.
If teammates are shopping, their items arrive in a few seconds. Waiting for them costs less than the ward you wanted.
Use the wards you can place safely: over a wall, or into brush you can already see. Deep wards go down when two of you walk together.
check: Who on your team is actually next to you, which enemies are missing, and is your sweeper or control ward ready?
breaks: Wrong if you saw four or five enemies on the other side of the map a moment ago: then go deep quickly, it's safe.
basis: pro:Do not check brush alone while your team shops

when: after 20:00
asks: they're on baron, do we go
do we contest baron
they started baron, what now
should we walk in
say: Clear the waves, poke from outside the choke and go in only once it's low, or trade a tower if you can't see them.
more: Teams often start it to pull you through a narrow, dark entrance. Walking in early gives them the fight they set up for.
If you wait at range, they must choose: keep hitting it and take your poke, or turn and walk at you. Either way the fight starts on your terms.
Your jungler should hover for the Smite only when the rest of you can follow. A jungler alone in the pit is the pick they were waiting for.
check: Do you have a ward on the pit, how fast are they killing it, and where are your side waves?
breaks: Wrong if they have real damage and it's dropping fast: then go in together at once, or accept it and take what you can elsewhere.
basis: pro:Decline the bait at the choke

asks: what do I do in fights as tank
who do I go on
do I peel or dive
what's my job in teamfights
say: Run at their carry to force his Flash and make them all turn on you, or stand in front of yours if they dive first.
more: You don't have to kill the carry. Every second their team spends dealing with you is a second your damage dealers hit for free.
It works when your team has something to do meanwhile, like killing a flanker. If they only watch, you die for nothing.
Go in after their key crowd control has been used on someone else. A tank who is chain-stunned at the start buys no time.
check: Is your team close enough to fight while you're in, and has their main stun or knock-up been used?
breaks: Wrong if their divers are already on your carry: turn around and peel, because a dead carry makes your dive pointless.
basis: pro:The tank who makes five people look at him

when: your team is mostly short-range and the enemy has two wave-clear mages
asks: how do we win this
what's our plan
what's our win condition
how do we close
we can't take towers
say: You can't siege into their wave clear, so fight at dragons and Baron where they must come out, or split a side to pull one away.
more: A short-range team loses health for nothing in front of a tower. At a pit the defenders have to walk to you, and your engage reaches them.
That makes every spawn a deadline. Be there first with waves pushed, because arriving second means walking through their poke.
If the game stalls with no objective up, don't stand mid. Farm, keep vision, and wait for the next timer.
check: When does the next dragon or Baron spawn, and which of your waves will be pushed by then?
breaks: Wrong if you are far ahead in items: then their wave clear only holds briefly and a slow siege with Baron buff works.
basis: pro:A team that cannot siege fights at the pits

asks: they're coming to dragon, what do I do
do I fight them or go to the pit
two of them are rotating
should I hold them off
say: Stand between them and the pit and stall with your defensive tools, or fall back into the pit if a third enemy shows.
more: Your job is seconds, not kills. If the enemy arrives after the Smite, the objective is yours and they have walked into your whole team.
Use dashes, stealth or slows to stay annoying without committing. Dying is acceptable only if the dragon finishes and your team gets the one who killed you.
If you can't delay them, joining the pit beats a half-fight outside it. Then everyone burns it down together.
check: How low is the objective, how many enemies are coming, and is your own escape up?
breaks: Wrong if you're low or have no escape: go into the pit and help finish, because a free kill on you starts their fight.
basis: pro:One player buys the seconds for the Smite

when: Teleport is one of your spells and a dragon spawns within a minute
asks: do I keep pushing or group
dragon's coming, I'm top
tower or dragon
should I tp to dragon
say: Finish the tower first if it's nearly dead, then Teleport to the fight, or leave now if this dragon is soul point.
more: A tower plus arriving on time is the best case, and Teleport makes it possible. The risk is channeling late and landing after the first kill.
If the dragon is only their first or second, your team can also just give it. A tower for an early dragon is a fair trade.
Tell your team which it is before the spawn. Four players who think you're coming will start a fight you never reach.
check: How much health is on the tower, is your Teleport actually up, and how many dragons does each team have?
breaks: Wrong if their side laner has Teleport and yours is down: you can't match him, so walk to the team early.
basis: pro:Tower first, then Teleport, or give the dragon

when: an enemy assassin has the most kills on their team
asks: how do we deal with their assassin
he keeps one-shotting our carry
who do I focus
what do I do when he jumps in
say: Everyone hits the assassin the moment he jumps in so he must leave, or stay grouped tight and deny the angle if you lack damage.
more: An assassin wins by being ignored for a moment. If the first thing he meets is crowd control and everyone's damage, he has to use his escape to live.
You don't need the kill. Forcing his defensive ultimate early means he's out of the fight while the rest of his team is still in it.
This only works if you stand close enough to help each other. Carries spread across the jungle are separate targets.
check: Where is he likely to come from, is that brush warded, and who holds the crowd control to answer him?
breaks: Wrong if their front line is also on top of you: deal with whoever is nearest and keep walking back.
basis: pro:Make the assassin spend his escape first

when: the enemy team has two or more champions who dive
asks: what do I build first
they keep diving me, what do I buy
damage or health first
should I build tanky
say: Buy a health item first so their burst no longer kills you, or go damage first if nobody on their team can reach you.
more: Against an assassin and a diving jungler, extra health turns their kill into a lost trade. You then push the wave while they recover.
Lane push is what it really buys. A mage who can stand in lane has priority, and priority decides who gets to the river first.
The cost is real: your damage comes later, so in mid-game fights your team has to carry more of it.
check: Who on their team can actually reach you, and how close are you to finishing either item?
breaks: Wrong if you are already ahead and they have no reliable way onto you: damage first ends fights before they start.
basis: pro:Health first against a dive team

when: the enemy team has three or more champions who dive
asks: I keep getting one shot
what do I buy against all this dive
do I build defensive
third item, what should I get
say: Take one defensive item now so you survive the first jump, or stay full damage only if your team has two real peelers.
more: Damage you never get to deal is worth nothing. One item with health or a shield often adds more damage over a fight than another damage item, because you stay alive to attack.
Positioning matters more than the item: stay behind your front line and hit the nearest target. The item covers the one time someone gets through.
Later, when their divers have items too, that defensive slot is what lets you play the last fights at all.
check: Which of their divers has Flash or a dash ready, and which teammates can actually stop them?
breaks: Wrong if their front line is too tanky to kill without full damage: keep the damage and stand further back instead.
basis: pro:A carry who lives deals the damage

when: after 8:00, grubs are alive and the enemy jungler is ahead of you in level
asks: they're on grubs, can I do anything
do I contest grubs
should I try to steal a grub
they're taking grubs and I'm behind
say: Sneak one grub from the far side of the pit with Smite and leave, or take the dragon if their bot lane went up too.
more: Grubs are separate monsters and they don't respawn. Taking one denies them the full set without a fight you would lose.
Come in from the side they aren't watching and leave the moment Smite lands. Staying for another is how a small win becomes a death.
If more of them are top than you expected, the bottom half is empty. A dragon for part of the grubs is a good deal.
check: Is a grub low enough to Smite, which side of the pit are they standing on, and who is still in bot lane?
breaks: Wrong if their mid and top both have push: you get collapsed on over the wall. Go straight to the other side of the map.
basis: pro:Steal one grub and walk away

when: a dragon spawns within 90 seconds
asks: how do we set up for dragon
what do I do before dragon
should I give my carry farm
our carry needs gold
say: Give your carry the next camp or wave so the item's finished before the spawn, or keep it and delay the fight if he's far off.
more: A carry a little short of a big item is weaker for the whole fight. One camp or a buff handed over a minute early can be that item.
It costs you a little, and it only works if he recalls and returns in time. Ping the camp and the timer so he knows why.
If he's a whole component away, no gift fixes it. Then stall, or give this dragon and fight the next one.
check: How much gold does your carry need, does he have time to recall, and which camp is up near him?
breaks: Wrong if you are the one a few gold from a spike that matters more, like a fed jungler: keep the camp.
basis: pro:Hand the carry his item before the spawn

asks: who do I hit in fights
should I go for their carry
their tank's on me, what do I do
how do I teamfight as adc
say: Hit whoever is closest and keep walking back, or step forward on their carry only after their divers have used everything.
more: Their tanks want you to walk past them to reach the back line. Shooting the tank in front of you from max range is slow, but it's damage you actually deal.
Fights turn when the front line falls or runs out of spells. That's your moment to move up, with nobody left who can jump you.
Stay on the opposite side of the fight from their flanker. If your team splits into two groups, be in the one with the peel.
check: Where is their flanker or assassin, which dashes and stuns have you seen used, and who on your team is next to you?
breaks: Wrong if their carry is caught and stunned in your range: switch to him at once, because killing him ends the fight.
basis: pro:Shoot the tank in front of you

when: the enemy killed Baron in the last three minutes
asks: they have baron, what do we do
how do we defend baron
do we fight them
they're sieging with baron
say: Clear waves from inside your base and give the outer towers, or fight only if someone walks past their minions alone.
more: Baron buff ends on a timer. A team that loses two towers but no inhibitor and no players has survived it.
The buffed minions are the danger, so kill them first with your wave clear. Without the wave, they have to dive towers to continue.
Forcing a fight outside the base is what they want. It turns a few towers into an inhibitor or the game.
check: Who on your team clears waves fastest, how long is left on the buff, and is a soul or elder dragon coming next?
breaks: Wrong if they split up to push three lanes and one of them is far from help: collapse on that one player together.
basis: pro:Sit out the Baron and give the outer towers

when: your health is low
asks: big wave's dying at my tower
can I walk up for the wave
I'm low but there's a huge wave
do I go get the minions
say: Give the wave and recall if he can all-in you at the tower, or walk up only with your jungler next to you.
more: Watching a full wave die hurts, but a death adds his kill gold and the next wave on top. One wave is recoverable, and a kill plus two waves can be the lane.
A laner waiting just outside your tower with his ultimate up is there for exactly this. He wants you to step forward for the cannon minion.
Recall, buy, and come back to a wave that pushes toward you. That's where you take the farm back safely.
check: Does he have his ultimate and Flash, how much health do you have, and is your jungler close?
breaks: Wrong if he just used his main abilities on the wave: then walk up and take what you can before they come back.
basis: pro:The wave is not worth the walk

when: your team is ahead in kills and the enemy outer mid tower is down
asks: we're ahead, how do we push
what do we do with the lead
do we group or split
how do we take more towers
say: Send your two safest players to the side lanes and keep three mid, or stay as five if nobody can escape a collapse.
more: Three pushing lanes make the losing team choose which tower to give. The side players should be the ones with Flash, a dash or Teleport, not just the strongest fighters.
The three in the middle don't fight. They hold the wave and watch for whoever leaves to answer a side lane, then press the other one.
It sets up Baron: once they're stretched across three lanes, whoever shows in a side lane is too far away to contest.
check: Who on your team has an escape and Teleport, and how many enemies can you see on the map?
breaks: Wrong if their team has strong pick tools and you have no vision in their jungle: push only to the river and group for objectives.
basis: pro:Two safe side lanes and three in the middle

asks: their top is split pushing, who goes
how many do we send to stop him
do I go kill the split pusher
he's taking our tower
say: Send one player who clears the wave from range and holds the tower, or collapse with three only if nothing's spawning soon.
more: A tanky split pusher takes a long time to kill. Three players spending that time on him is exactly what his team wants at the other end of the map.
Clearing the wave is enough. Without minions he must dive a tower alone, and most split pushers won't.
If you do collapse, check the clock first. Killing him shortly before a dragon is good. Chasing him while they take Baron is not.
check: What can the other four enemies take while you are there, and how long would he take to kill?
breaks: Wrong if he's squishy and has no Flash: then two of you kill him fast and the trade is yours.
basis: pro:Three players for one tank is a bad price

when: before 6:00
asks: I just backed, do I go back bot
should I roam top
can I gank another lane as support
where do I go after recall
say: Walk to top or mid with your jungler on the way back from base, or return bot if your carry is pushed up alone.
more: Coming out of base, the lanes are a similar walk. A third player arriving in a solo lane this early is very hard to survive.
Go with the jungler, not alone: your crowd control plus his damage is what makes it a kill and not just a visit.
Your carry pays for it with a wave or two alone. It's worth it when the lane you help is the one your team needs ahead.
check: Where is your jungler heading, is your carry's wave safe near his tower, and is the target lane pushed toward your side?
breaks: Wrong if their bot lane has kill pressure on your carry alone: go back, because one death there gives up the plates too.
basis: pro:Leave base for a different lane

asks: our ult missed, do we still fight
engage failed, what now
we used everything and nobody died
do we keep contesting
say: Your opener didn't kill, so back off and give it, or go again only once your big cooldowns return and theirs are down.
more: A pick team is strongest in the first second of a fight. After a missed opener, the other team has all its spells and you have none.
Contesting anyway is how a lost objective becomes a lost objective plus two kills. Leaving costs only the objective.
Use the time: push a side wave, take their camps, and set up the same engage for the next spawn with vision down first.
check: Which of your ultimates are down, did they use any of their answers, and can you afford to lose this objective?
breaks: Wrong if it's their soul dragon or an elder: then you fight anyway, but wait for them to start it and go for the Smite.
basis: pro:When the opener misses, leave

when: after 20:00 and your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: can we sneak baron
should we rush baron
we can't win fights, baron?
is a baron flip worth it
say: Rush Baron only when they're all seen far away and you hold Smite, or keep clearing waves if one of them is missing.
more: A team that loses every full fight has few ways back, and a fast Baron is one. It works because they don't believe you'll try it.
Bring everyone and commit. A half-started Baron leaves you low on health in a pit, which is the worst place to be found.
Even a secured Baron can cost a player on the way out. Agree beforehand that you leave through your own jungle as soon as it dies.
check: Where did each enemy last show, do they have a ward on the pit, and does your team kill Baron quickly?
breaks: Wrong if your damage is low and it takes long: they arrive with it half done and win both the fight and Baron. Defend and wait for a pick.
basis: pro:The quiet Baron when you cannot win the fight

when: a dragon or Baron spawns within 90 seconds
asks: where do I ward
when do I ward for dragon
how do we get vision control
should I sweep now
say: Wait until two of your lanes are pushing, then ward their jungle entrances together, or ward your own side if lanes are stuck.
more: Vision follows waves. With mid and a side lane pushed, their laners are under towers and can't punish you for walking into the river.
Wards at their jungle entrances show which way they come. Then they must walk a narrow, lit path into a team that's already waiting.
If your lanes are pushed in, deep wards just get you killed. Put them where you will defend from and give up the far entrances.
check: Which waves are past the middle, where are their support and jungler, and how many control wards does your team have?
breaks: Wrong if they already hold the river with numbers: don't contest it ward by ward. Push a far wave and trade.
basis: pro:Push the waves, then place the wards

when: before 3:00
asks: when do I ward
should I ward river now
where does my first ward go
do I ward at level one
say: Keep your ward until their jungler's first clear is nearly done, or place it now if you plan to shove from level one.
more: A full clear takes a jungler to about level 4, and the first river crabs spawn at 2:55. The first real gank on bot usually comes around then.
A ward placed at the very start runs out just when it's needed. Holding it covers the window that actually kills lanes.
The exception is a lane that fights at levels 1 and 2. If you push that early, a short clear into your lane is likely, so the ward goes down first.
check: Are you pushing or being pushed, and did either jungler show on the top or bottom half at the start?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler ganks early and started on your side: ward the river brush as soon as you pass the middle.
basis: pro:Save the ward for the first gank window

when: your health is low
asks: do I flash
should I flash away
I'm caught, do I use flash
flash or just die
say: Flash only if it clearly gets you out, or hold it and die with it up if they can follow anyway.
more: A Flash that delays a death by a second is the worst outcome: you lose the kill and the next few minutes of safety as well.
Coming back to lane with Flash up, you can still play the wave and survive the next gank. Without it, you're the target every time their jungler passes.
Use it early or not at all. Flashing before the crowd control lands works. Flashing after it, into another dash, doesn't.
check: Do they still have a dash, a stun or their own Flash to follow, and how far is your tower?
breaks: Wrong if you carry a big shutdown or an objective is about to spawn: then try everything, Flash included, to live.
basis: pro:Keep Flash when you die either way

asks: how do we engage
should I flank
we keep losing fights when we go in
do we all go at once
say: Go in from one side together on one target, or send a single flanker only if he waits for the front to start first.
more: A dive team arriving from four directions fights four small fights. The first one in is dead before the others land.
One flanker is enough to threaten the back line. His job is to arrive second, when their peel has been used on your front.
Decide the target before the fight. Everyone's ultimate on the same player kills. Spread over three players, nobody dies.
check: Is everyone close enough to arrive within a moment of each other, and which enemy has no Flash?
breaks: Wrong if they have strong area damage and you'd be clumped in a choke: spread a little on entry, but still pick one target.
basis: pro:Four angles are four small fights

when: you have two or more kills before 10:00
asks: I'm fed bot, now what
where do I go with this lead
should I stay bot
do I rotate mid
say: Move to mid where the lane's short and ganks are harder, or stay bot only while their jungler is showing on the top side.
more: A fed carry in a long side lane is their jungler's best target. Mid is shorter, closer to your towers, and next to both rivers.
From mid you clear the wave fast and arrive first at dragon or grubs. Your mid laner takes the side lane, where a solo champion is usually safer.
Ask for the swap, don't just walk in. Two players sharing one wave wastes the gold you were ahead by.
check: Has your outer bot tower or theirs fallen, where is their jungler, and will your mid laner agree to swap?
breaks: Wrong if your mid laner can't survive the side lane matchup: stay bot together with vision and take plates instead.
basis: pro:Move the fed carry to the short lane

when: you died in the last 30 seconds and it is before 6:00
asks: I died to a gank, can I still play the lane
do I tp back
he got first blood, how do I play now
is my lane lost
say: Teleport back and take the wave while he still holds the gold unspent, or walk and save Teleport if the wave's coming to you.
more: A kill is only numbers on the scoreboard until he recalls. If he stayed in lane, he fights on the same items as before.
The danger starts after his first recall. From then on, trade less, keep the wave near your tower and expect another gank.
Teleporting keeps your experience level now, but leaves you without it for a few minutes. Don't be low on health in that window.
check: Did he recall after the kill, which way is the wave heading, and is their jungler still top side?
breaks: Wrong if he has already bought and the wave is held at his tower: don't walk into it. Farm what reaches you and ask for help.
basis: pro:He has the kill but not the item yet

when: you have died twice or more and your lane opponent is ahead in level
asks: I'm so behind top, what do I do
he's fed, I can't lane
how do I stop feeding
should I give up the tower
say: Stop defending the wave: farm what reaches your tower and give the plates, or leave to mid for experience if he dives.
more: The third and fourth deaths are what make a fed top laner unstoppable. A tower is a fixed amount of gold, and your deaths have no limit.
You can't fix the wave alone against a stronger champion with jungle help near. If nobody comes to break it, don't walk past your tower.
Your value comes later: a tank or utility champion with levels still does its job in fights. Protect your experience first.
check: Is anyone on your team coming to help, how many plates are left, and where are their jungler and support?
breaks: Wrong if your jungler and mid are both nearby with the wave on your side: then fight with numbers and reset the lane.
basis: pro:Give the tower before the third death

when: after 20:00 and your team has more dragons but fewer kills
asks: they're starting baron and we're scaling
do we have to fight
can we just farm
they keep forcing us to fight
say: Send your wave clear to poke the pit and stall, or trade towers on the far side if your carry would have to walk in.
more: They start Baron because your carry out-scales them. The point is to make him walk through a dark river while they still have the stronger dive.
Your dragons mean you aren't the one on a clock. Every minute without a fight is another piece of an item for the carry.
What you can't do is nothing. Either slow it from range so they turn and lose time, or take something of similar size while they finish.
check: Does your carry have Flash, is the path to the pit warded, and what is open on the other side?
breaks: Wrong if Baron would let them end with your inhibitors already down: then contest as five and go for the Smite.
basis: pro:They start Baron to make your carry walk

asks: when do I use condemn
how do I teamfight as vayne
should I condemn their tank
how do I not die in fights
say: Hold Condemn for whoever gets through to you and pin them to a wall, or use it forward only when nobody can reach you.
more: Your team's crowd control handles the first divers. Condemn is for the one who slips past, and it stuns if he hits terrain.
Stand where a wall is behind the path he has to take. Terrain a teammate creates can work too. A stun on the diver usually ends his attempt.
Without Condemn you rely on Tumble alone. Against a team with little hard crowd control that's enough, and you can spend Condemn on damage.
check: Which enemy is trying to reach you, and is there a wall or created terrain behind him?
breaks: Wrong if their diver is already locked down by your team: use Condemn for the extra damage and keep attacking.
basis: pro:Keep the peel button for whoever gets through

when: a kill happened in a side lane in the last 60 seconds and it is before 6:00
asks: do I go back to that lane
where's their jungler going next
should I gank the same lane again
bot just fought, do I stay
say: Clear one camp nearby and come back to that lane, because their jungler will too, or cross the map if it's now pushed to your tower.
more: After an early skirmish the laners are low, missing summoner spells and often a level apart. That lane stays the best target on the map for the next minute.
Their jungler knows it as well. Being there first turns his repeat gank into your counter-gank, with your laners already expecting it.
If the wave ends up under your tower, your laners are safe without you, and the far side of the map is where your time pays.
check: Which summoner spells were used, where is the wave, and which of your camps are up on that side?
breaks: Wrong if you're low on health yourself or clearly behind his level: recall first, or you are the one who dies there.
basis: pro:Go back to the lane that just fought

when: your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: how do we come back
should we try to pick their carry
we keep dying trying to catch someone
what do we do when we're this behind
say: Stop hunting their fed carry: hold waves under towers and wait for someone to overstep, or take a far camp or tower while they group.
more: When three of them are rich, killing one doesn't win the fight that follows. The attempts mostly hand them more gold.
A leading team gets impatient and dives. The comeback usually starts from their mistake under your tower, not from your pick in their jungle.
Until then, every wave you collect safely closes the gap. Shutdown gold arrives when they come to you.
check: Which enemies carry shutdowns, where is your vision, and can you clear waves without stepping past your towers?
breaks: Wrong if only one enemy is fed and the rest are weak: then a pick on him with everything you have is the right gamble.
basis: pro:One pick does not beat three rich enemies

when: after 8:00 and grubs are alive
asks: do I finish grubs
last grub or go
their jungler's in my jungle, do I stay on grubs
should I leave the last grub
say: Take the grubs already low and go defend your camps if their jungler's missing, or finish the set if he just showed bot.
more: While you are in the pit, their jungler isn't standing still. If he isn't contesting, he is usually eating your other half or setting up a gank.
Most of the grubs plus your own camps is worth more than the full set and an empty jungle. The last one is also the one they like to steal.
The full set matters most for teams that plan to break towers early. If that's your plan, ask a laner to hold the pit while you finish.
check: Where was their jungler last seen, which of your camps are up, and can anyone on your team guard the pit?
breaks: Wrong if your laners have push and can hold the pit: finish them all, since grubs do not respawn.
basis: pro:Part of the grubs and your camps beat the full set

asks: who do I engage on
who's the target
everyone has an escape, who do I go
how do I start the fight
say: Fake the engage to draw out their shield or cleanse, then go on that player, or pick whoever has no Flash.
more: Against a team where every carry has an answer, the first engage rarely kills. Its real job is to make someone press the button.
Call out which one was used. The second engage, on the player with nothing left, is the one your team follows.
If nobody bites, don't force it into a full-health tank. Keep the threat alive and let waves and vision do the work.
check: Which enemy has used Flash, a spell shield or an untargetable ability in the last minute?
breaks: Wrong if an objective is about to die: there's no time for two tries, so go on whoever is closest to it.
basis: pro:Dive the player who just used the answer

when: an ally died in the last 10 seconds
asks: he got caught, do we fight
should I go in to save him
teammate's dead, do we still go
do we turn or leave
say: Leave now and give what they came for, or turn only if they burned their ultimates and your whole team is next to you.
more: Walking in to save or avenge a caught teammate is how one death becomes three. They are grouped and expecting it.
Count the spells. If they used several ultimates on one player and yours are up, being one short can be an even fight for a few seconds.
If you leave, use the time: push a far wave, or ward your side of the objective they're about to take.
check: How many ultimates did they use, who on your team is close, and how long is your teammate's death timer?
breaks: Wrong if the caught player is still alive with only one enemy on him: then help, because the numbers are yours.
basis: pro:One caught is one lost, not three

when: your team killed the Rift Herald in the last three minutes and is behind in kills
asks: I've still got herald
when do I drop herald
we're behind, where does herald go
should I wait for a better moment
say: Use Herald now on whichever tower has the fewest defenders, or pair it with a pushed side wave if mid is guarded.
more: When you're behind, the perfect moment rarely comes and the Herald expires unused. Any tower's gold helps your team buy back into the game.
A side tower with one defender falls. A mid tower with three defenders usually kills the Herald before it charges.
Tell the lane you're coming so the wave arrives with it. Alone, the Herald gets focused down. With minions, the tower shoots them first.
check: Which towers are weakest, how many enemies show on the map, and how long have you been holding it?
breaks: Wrong if a dragon fight is moments away and you can contest: drop it mid then, so they must answer two places.
basis: pro:A Herald in your pocket pays nothing

asks: do I take the kill
should I leave kills for the carry
who should get the gold
is it bad if I get the kills
say: Leave the last hit for your carry when the kill is certain, or take it yourself rather than risk him escaping.
more: Gold does more on a champion who scales with items. Kills on a tank or a support win the lane and not much beyond it.
A jungler with early kills is still useful: you buy sooner and control the next objectives. Just know that lead ends earlier than a carry's would.
Never lose a kill trying to give it away. A secured kill on the wrong player beats a lost one on the right player.
check: Is the target certain to die, and is your carry in range to finish?
breaks: Wrong if you're a carry jungler your team is built around: take everything you can.
basis: pro:Put the kill on the champion that spends it best

when: after 14:00 and your top or mid laner does not have Teleport
asks: should we fight now
do we start this fight
our top's in a side lane, do we go
is it four v five
say: Wait: your side laner can't arrive, so hold until he walks over, or fight right away only if you've caught someone alone.
more: Starting a fight while one of you is in a far lane with no Teleport is choosing to be one short. Their side laner may have his and join.
The side push is still useful, because it pulls someone. Check that one of them actually left before you commit.
If you must fight now, do it close to the lane he is in, so he can walk into it.
check: Where is your side laner, did an enemy go to match him, and whose Teleport is up?
breaks: Wrong if their side laner is also far away without Teleport: then the numbers are even and a pick is yours to take.
basis: pro:One short because a side laner cannot teleport

when: after 10:00
asks: can I take their camps
is it safe to invade bot side
should I steal their gromp
can I counter jungle now
say: Check which enemies are in the lane next to that camp first, then take it, or skip it if their duo has moved there.
more: After the first towers fall, lanes get reassigned. The side that had one top laner next to it may now have a carry and a support.
Two players reach you faster than one and bring crowd control. A camp is never worth that.
The good invade is beside a lane your team has pushed in, or right after you see their duo on the other side of the map.
check: Who is in the nearest lane right now, is that wave pushed toward you, and is your escape up?
breaks: Wrong if you just saw four of them on the far side: take the whole quadrant and ward it on the way out.
basis: pro:The lane beside their jungle may have changed

when: after 14:00 and no dragon or Baron spawns within two minutes
asks: should I shove this wave
do I push side or farm it slow
nothing's up, what do I do
how do I farm side lane safely
say: Nothing's spawning, so last-hit and let the wave build on your side, or shove it fast if your team needs someone pulled away.
more: Shoving has a purpose: it frees you to move. With nowhere to go, a shoved wave just leaves you standing far up a lane.
A slow wave on your half is safe gold, and it becomes a big push later that their team has to answer.
Switch the moment a timer gets close. The wave you built crashes just as you need to leave for the pit.
check: How long until the next dragon or Baron, where is their jungler, and how far up the lane are you standing?
breaks: Wrong if an objective spawns sooner than you thought: push hard at once and walk over with your team.
basis: pro:With nothing spawning, let the wave build

when: a dragon or Baron spawns within a minute
asks: when do we go to dragon
how early do we set up
our team can't face check
should we be there first
say: Be at the pit half a minute early with wards down, or give it if they're already sitting in the brush.
more: A team of ranged carries and catch supports can't walk into dark brush. Whoever sets up first decides who has to face-check.
From your own setup, hooks and skill shots land on people walking in a straight line toward you. Arriving second, you're the ones being hit.
Getting there early needs waves pushed and recalls finished about a minute before. Plan backwards from the spawn.
check: Are your waves pushed, has everyone finished shopping, and does anyone on your team have the health to check a brush?
breaks: Wrong if you have a tank who can walk in first safely: then arriving at the same time is fine, and he leads.
basis: pro:If nobody can face-check, be there first

when: your team is behind in dragons and kills
asks: how do we get a pick
where do we look for a fight
we need something to happen
we can't contest anything, what now
say: Wait in brush on the path to their next buff with crowd control ready, or just clear waves if you don't have vision there.
more: Buffs respawn five minutes after they die, and a leading jungler often walks to them alone and relaxed. It's one of the few predictable moves a winning team makes.
Killing the jungler does more than give gold. With no Smite on their side, the next dragon or Baron is yours to start.
Go as two or three with a sweeper, set up before the buff is due, and leave if they show numbers. Don't sit there for minutes.
check: When did their buff last die, is the brush clear of wards, and where are their laners?
breaks: Wrong if they have wards on their own entrances and move as a group: you're walking into them. Defend and wait instead.
basis: pro:Wait where their jungler has to walk

when: the enemy team has two or more champions who heal
asks: should I buy anti-heal
they heal so much
who buys grievous wounds
what do we do about all this healing
say: Buy healing reduction on whoever hits their whole team most often, or skip it yourself if you only reach one target.
more: Healing reduction only works while it's applied. A mage with area spells keeps it on several enemies at once. A front-line fighter keeps it on one.
One good carrier of it is enough. Three people buying it means three people missing damage.
Buy the cheap component first if you're in the middle of another item. It does most of the job and the upgrade can wait.
check: Who on your team has area damage that lands every fight, and who on theirs is doing the healing?
breaks: Wrong if their healing comes from one champion who dies early in fights: kill him first and keep the item slot.
basis: pro:Healing reduction on the player who hits everyone

when: before 6:00
asks: where's their jungler
am I safe to push top
their support's missing
can I trade now
say: If their support isn't showing bot, play at your tower as if three are coming, or trade freely once he's seen back in lane.
more: A support who was forced to recall sometimes walks top with the jungler and skips bot. Two extra players this early isn't survivable.
It costs them their carry's safety, so it tends to happen when their bot wave is already at their tower. That's the cue to watch for.
Losing a few minions while you wait is the price. Once the support shows bot again, you know the top side is only the jungler.
check: Can you see their support on the map, where is your wave, and did your bot lane ping him missing?
breaks: Wrong if your own jungler is top side with you: hold the wave in the middle and let them walk into even numbers.
basis: pro:A missing support can be in your lane too

asks: what's my job as poppy
when do I use my W
how do I stop their divers
who do I stand next to
say: Stand beside your carry and save Steadfast Presence for the dash onto him, or use it to chase only when their dashes are down.
more: Steadfast Presence stops enemy dashes around you. Against a team that has to dash to reach your back line, one well-timed use can end their engage.
The hard part is waiting. If you spend it running at someone, the diver goes in the moment after.
Heroic Charge and Keeper's Verdict do the rest: stun the one who came in against a wall, or knock the next ones far away.
check: Which enemies need a dash to engage, and have they used it yet?
breaks: Wrong if their threats are ranged and never dash: then play forward and look for wall stuns instead.
basis: pro:Hold the anti-dash for the dive

asks: what's our win condition
who do we play around
how do we win fights
who's our carry
say: Count who deals your damage: with only two, the team stands around them, or with three or more you can dive freely.
more: A team with two damage dealers loses the fight when either one dies early. Everyone else's job is to keep those two attacking.
The enemy knows it too and will send everything at them. Expect the dive and stand close enough to answer it.
With three threats, losing one still leaves a fight. That's when your tanks can go deep, because someone behind them still kills.
check: Which of your teammates actually have items and kills, and which enemy is most likely to reach them?
breaks: Wrong if one of the two is far behind: then you really have one carry, and you fight only when he is in position.
basis: pro:Count your damage threats

when: you are level 5 and it is between 6:30 and 8:00
asks: grubs are coming, do I go now
should I get six first
farm or set up for grubs
do I need my ult for grubs
say: Take the camps that get you to six on the way and arrive with your ultimate, or go early to ward if you're already close.
more: Grubs open at 8:00 and the first fight there is often decided by who has an ultimate. A level 5 jungler at the pit mostly watches.
Plan the route so your last camp before the spawn is on the top side. Then level 6 and position come together.
If their jungler is already 6 and you can't be, say so. Your team can send a laner early or take the dragon instead.
check: How much experience do you need, which camps are up on the way, and what level is their jungler?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is dead or seen bot: go now at level 5, because a free start beats a level.
basis: pro:Arrive at grubs with the ultimate

when: you completed your first item in the last minute and your lane opponent has not
asks: I just got my item, can I fight
should I trade now
am I stronger than him
do I look for a fight
say: Fight now while he's still on components: force the trade in lane, or call a river skirmish if he won't walk up.
more: A completed item against components is the clearest edge in the lane phase, and it lasts only until his next recall.
If he hides under tower, the edge still works elsewhere. Shove the wave and show up at a crab, a camp fight or the next objective with it.
Afterwards the lane evens out again, so use the window for something that stays: plates, a kill or a dragon.
check: Did he recall recently, is his jungler near, and is the wave somewhere you can fight on?
breaks: Wrong if he's a level or two ahead: the item doesn't cover that. Trade short and wait for your jungler.
basis: pro:The minute after your first item

when: two or more allies died in the last 30 seconds
asks: where do I farm now
can I take my blue
we lost the fight, what do I do
is my jungle safe
say: Farm the camps nearest your base first and leave the buff by the river, or take it only with a laner beside you.
more: After a won fight, the other team walks into your jungle with nothing to fear. The buff nearest the fight is where their jungler waits.
Jumping a wall into a dark camp alone turns a lost fight into a lost fight plus your death and your buff.
Inner camps are slower gold but safe. By the time they respawn your team is alive again and you can clear outward together.
check: Where did the fight end, which enemies are still alive nearby, and is there a ward on the buff?
breaks: Wrong if you saw them recall or go to an objective on the other side: then take the buff quickly before they come back.
basis: pro:After a lost fight your buff is watched

when: before 4:00
asks: can I steal their buff
should I invade their blue
do I go for the buff steal
is it worth invading now
say: Go only if you can Smite and leave over a wall, or skip it and take the crab if their lane's already walking over.
more: A buff steal is a hit and run. The moment Smite lands, you leave. Staying to fight is what costs Flash or your life.
Even a clean steal can cost Flash. Count that in: for the next few minutes you gank and duel without it, so plan to farm.
It pays when it leaves their jungler without a buff for his first ganks and slows his way to level 6.
check: Did you cross a ward on the way in, which lane is nearer the buff, and is your Smite up?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler duels better and their laners have push: you lose the Smite and the fight. Mirror his clear and take your crab.
basis: pro:A buff steal is a hit and run

when: your lane opponent is a melee tank and you are ranged
asks: how do I lane against this tank
can I keep poking him
he keeps jumping on me
do I push or freeze top
say: Poke him off the wave but stay outside his dash when your Flash is down, or hold the wave near your tower.
more: You win this lane on health and farm, not kills. He wins it with one engage that lands while you step up for a minion.
Watch which ability he saves. Tanks often open with the one you weren't expecting, so keep distance from all of them when you can't Flash.
A pushed wave makes you the gank target and gives him the long lane to run you down. Near your tower, his engage reaches nothing.

asks: I've got no flash, how do I lane

he keeps looking for me without flash

more: Without Flash, every engage tool they have lands. Their mid and jungler know your timer and will come back for the repeat.

asks: I'm losing mid, what do I do
should I roam or keep farming
I can't win this lane
how do I get back into the game from mid
say: Shove one wave and walk to a side lane with your ultimate, or stay and farm safely if both side lanes are pushed up.
more: A lane you can't win doesn't have to be the whole game. A kill or a burned Flash in a side lane helps your team more than a few even trades.
It costs minions at your tower, so make the trip short and only when the target lane is near your side.
Your opponent has to choose: follow and lose his lead in farm, or stay and let his side lane be outnumbered.
check: Which side lane is pushed toward your tower, is your ultimate up, and will their mid follow you?
breaks: Wrong if their mid shoves faster and takes plates every time you leave: farm under tower and wait for your jungler.
